split_policy.method: random shuffle of account_id with fixed seed, computed before the human-reference manifold is built; the human reference is derived only from label==0 accounts whose split is 'train'

calibration_note: Synthetic feature distributions inspired by social bot and human behavioral patterns. Human reference manifold estimated from synthetic training-split humans only. Humanization targets are sampled as COMPLETE human rows (preserving cross-feature correlation), not per-feature independent samples.
mean_feature_shift_caveat: mean_feature_shift (in window_metadata) is a descriptive per-feature displacement measure, not a calibrated or causal drift-magnitude metric. It can behave oddly for small-baseline, large-count features (e.g. a 1->20 change looks huge; a 10,000->12,000 change looks small despite being operationally larger). Do not use it as ground truth for how 'harmful' drift is.
important_limitations: Synthetic benchmark, not real longitudinal social data.
Results must not be presented as real-world performance.
External empirical calibration should be reported separately.
Boundary-crossing validation (pre/post-drift F1 on a trained model) is a separate step that must be run before treating this dataset as containing 'harmful' drift by construction.
Core profile features (age/followers/friends/listed) evolve via monotonic organic growth only -- never toward a humanization target -- regardless of scenario.
Do not tune generator parameters against test-set F1, and do not use the test split to choose drift-aware thresholds.

validation_checks.human_reference_leakage_guard: human_reference is built only from label==0 & split=='train' accounts (906 accounts); no validation/test account statistics are used to construct drift targets.
